FISHING LICENCE · NORWAY

Norway fishing licence

Anglers aged 18 and above need the national fee payment for salmon, sea trout and migratory Arctic char in rivers and lakes. They also need the local water permit; ordinary freshwater fish require the local permission without that national fee.

Buy a licence online ↗Official rules ↗

Updated 2026-11-11

Who needs one

  • Anglers aged 18 and above who fish for migratory salmonids in freshwater must pay the national fee.
  • Freshwater anglers must obtain the water owner's permission.

Who doesn’t

  • Anglers under 18 do not pay the national fishing fee. Local permission can still be required.

Extra stamps and permits

  • Local fishing licence
    For the chosen river or lake, including when the national salmon fee is required.

Saltwater

Ordinary recreational sea angling does not require a fishing licence. Foreign visitors must use hand-held tackle and must not sell the catch.

Rules visitors should know

  • Stay at least 100 metres from fish farms when fishing.
  • Observe sea-fish minimum sizes.
  • In 2026, tourists may export up to 15 kg of sea fish twice a year only through a registered tourist-fishing business.
  • The export allowance requires the visitor to be at least 12 and carry the required documentation.

How to buy

Pay the national fee on the Environment Agency portal. Obtain the local licence from the owner or fishery.

Common license questions

Do I need a fishing licence in Norway?

Anglers aged 18 and above need the national fee payment for salmon, sea trout and migratory Arctic char in rivers and lakes. They also need the local water permit; ordinary freshwater fish require the local permission without that national fee.

Where do I buy a fishing licence in Norway?

Pay the national fee on the Environment Agency portal. Obtain the local licence from the owner or fishery.
